cards.front: Recall a key point about 3D Form and Sculpture Techniques
cards.back: Modelling builds up form by adding material (clay, plasticine); carving removes material to reveal form (wood, soap, stone).

cards.front: Recall a key point about 3D Form and Sculpture Techniques
cards.back: Casting creates multiples from a mould — plaster, latex, silicone; assemblage joins ready-made or found objects.

cards.front: Recall a key point about 3D Form and Sculpture Techniques
cards.back: Sculpture must be considered from ALL viewpoints — walk around it, photograph from multiple angles.

cards.front: Recall a key point about 3D Form and Sculpture Techniques
cards.back: Mass (solid volume), volume (enclosed space) and negative space (the spaces within and around) are key 3D concepts.

cards.front: What should you know about fine art exam tips?
cards.back: Photograph work from AT LEAST 4 angles. Show the making PROCESS — in-progress shots are essential evidence. Annotate with material names and technique vocabulary. Link to sculptors who use similar processes.

Students often make mistakes with this topic. Wrong: A sculpture is finished when it looks good from the front. Correct: Sculpture exists in three dimensions — it must be resolved from ALL angles. Walk around your work, photograph it from multiple viewpoints, and ensure it communicates from every position.

Experiment with at least two different 3D techniques (modelling, carving, casting, constructing). Document your process with photographs and annotations. Evaluate which technique best suits your intentions.

cards.front: Assessment Objective Focus: 3D Form and Sculpture Techniques
cards.back: AO1 — Knowledge: Demonstrate knowledge of 3D Form and Sculpture Techniques using appropriate art vocabulary. Identify techniques, materials and processes accurately.
